CALENDARIA.ClimateEditor.Presets.Instruc: Override weather behavior per zone and per season. Use the Season dropdown to select which season to edit. Weight sets a per-season override: an absolute number replaces the season base weight, a number with a + or - suffix adjusts it relatively (e.g. 8+ adds 8, 3- subtracts 3), 0 excludes the preset, and empty means no override. Temp Min/Max override the zone's base temperature when this weather is active. Use a + or - suffix for relative adjustments (e.g. 5+ is 5° warmer than base). HEROMANCER.App.Welcome.GM.StepApprovals: When players submit characters, a banner appears at the top of your screen. If you dismiss the banner, submissions are still available from the Pending Approvals Queue in the settings menu.
HEROMANCER.App.Welcome.GM.StepLevelUp: Grant a level-up by pressing Send Level Up on the group sheet header. A glowing Level Up button appears on the player's sheet near the rest buttons.

HEROMANCER.App.Welcome.Player.Heading: Getting Started
HEROMANCER.App.Welcome.Player.StepLaunch: Open Hero Mancer 2 from the Actor Directory header or by choosing Create with Hero Mancer 2 in the Create Actor dialog.
HEROMANCER.App.Welcome.Player.StepLevelU: When your GM grants a level-up, a glowing Level Up button appears on your sheet near your rest buttons. Click it to start.
HEROMANCER.App.Welcome.Player.StepSubmit: Press Create Character to finish. If your GM requires approval, the button reads Submit for Approval and the wizard locks until they review your submission. A banner shows the reason if it was rejected.
HEROMANCER.App.Welcome.Player.StepTabs: Fill out all the information you can on each tab and sub-tab before finalizing your character.

PEDDLER.Editor.HelpBody:
Dialogue trees

A tree is a set of nodes joined by choices. A visit starts at the entry node and follows choices until it reaches an End node.

  • Dialogue: the shopkeeper speaks lines, and each choice is a button.
  • Browse: a filtered item grid and the cart.
  • Inventory: the player picks one of their own items into a named variable.
  • Transaction: commits the cart, then branches by outcome.
  • Roll Table and Auto: branch without asking. One choice must carry no condition, as the fallback.
  • Goto: jumps to another node, or to another tree.
  • End: closes the visit.

A choice shows only while its Show When conditions hold, charges whatever sits in Cost, and runs its When Chosen effects once taken.

PEDDLER.Archetype.Blacksmith.Name: The Iron Oath
PEDDLER.Archetype.Blacksmith.Lines.greet: New face. Look all you like, but ask before you touch anything on that wall.
You're back. Knew the edge would bring you round.
Light purse. Mine was too, once. Look anyway.
So, what is it you're after?
PEDDLER.Archetype.Blacksmith.Lines.haggl: I make every piece by hand, and I don't knock coin off just because someone asked.
Ten percent off the wall too, since you'll be spreading my name. And not a word to anyone about what I charged you.
A village smith charges one, and their work bends the first time you swing it.
So it's {fee} now, and the wall costs you a tenth more. That's what the insult buys you.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Blacksmith.Lines.sharp: Sit down. It'll take as long as it takes.
Quiet today, so it's just me and the wheel.
There. Your {{session.vars.honed.name}}, honed sharp. Run your thumb along it, gently now.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Blacksmith.Ambient.bro: All handmade. You're paying for the hours and the steel that went into it.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Blacksmith.Lines.no-fu: The wall doesn't move on credit.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Blacksmith.Lines.farew: Look after it and it'll last you.
The wall keeps. I'm not going anywhere.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Blacksmith.Choices.gre: Put an edge on my blade
Put an edge on my blade, as agreed
Put an edge on my blade
{fee} for a whetstone and ten minutes?
PEDDLER.Archetype.Blacksmith.Choices.hag: {fee}, and I'll tell every sellsword on the road who put the edge on it
PEDDLER.Archetype.Apothecary.Name: The Bitter Root
PEDDLER.Archetype.Apothecary.Lines.greet: Hi! Um, welcome, mind the shelves, some of it bites back.
First time? Okay, don't be overwhelmed, it looks like a lot but I'll walk you through it.
Oh, it's you again, {{actor.name}}. Good, I remembered the last one worked.
So, um, what are you after? Are you well? You don't look unwell. Are you unwell?
PEDDLER.Archetype.Apothecary.Lines.intak: Right, tell me where it hurts, or, or what feels wrong, and I'll match it to something.
The master makes it all himself. It actually works, I swear, I have seen it work.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Apothecary.Lines.remed: A fever, okay. Willowbark and the blue draught, and you keep the fluids up, alright?
A wound. Right. Salve first, then the poultice, and please, please change the dressing daily.
Nerves. Yeah. I get that too, honestly. There's a calming tincture, it takes the edge off.
Not sure? That's fine, that's normal, we'll start gentle and see how you feel.
Come on, it's this way, I keep the good stuff where the light doesn't spoil it.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Apothecary.Ambient.fla: Anything you're already carrying, um, a bottle, a draught, whatever it is, just hand it here.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Apothecary.Lines.stead: Right, hold still, this bit stains and I have ruined two aprons this week.
Your {{session.vars.flask.name}}, cut with grey root and a thumb of honey so it goes down.
You'll be steady for about an hour. Please don't do anything stupid inside that hour.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Apothecary.Ambient.bro: Everything on this shelf is fresh, um, fresh enough, the dates are on the little tags.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Apothecary.Lines.no-fu: Oh, um, that's a little more than you've got on you, no worries, we can set some aside.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Apothecary.Lines.farew: Great choice, um, take it with food mostly, okay, feel better!
Oh, okay, no worries, come back if it gets worse, or, or better, either way.
Bye! Careful on the step, it wobbles.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Apothecary.Choices.int: I can't sleep, my nerves are shot
PEDDLER.Archetype.Apothecary.Choices.rem: Have you got something stronger for it?
PEDDLER.Archetype.Festival.Name: The Painted Wagon
PEDDLER.Archetype.Festival.Lines.greetin: Fresh, fresh, nothing on this board is stale!
Market day, and my own voice is coming back off the church!
Last hour, love, and I am not carting this lot home again!
Go on, look at the spread. Look at it.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Festival.Ambient.stall: Point at whatever takes your fancy, love, I'll have it bagged before you blink.
Enjoy it warm, love, that's how it's meant!
Go on, was there anything else caught your eye?
PEDDLER.Archetype.Festival.Lines.short.0: Save your coppers, duck, that one's dear today.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Festival.Lines.short.1: The day-old's half price and just as sweet.
Oh, you've just missed us, love. Stall's shut.
We're only out when the festival's on, weekends while the light's good.
Find me when the square's loud again and the corner loaf is yours.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Festival.Lines.farewel: Off you pop, love, and no sharing, you earned that!
No bother, love, come back when your belly grumbles!
The smell alone'll bring you back, mark me.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Caravan.Name: Wandering Wares
PEDDLER.Archetype.Caravan.Lines.greeting: Morning to you. I'm here till the sun's high and then I'm not.
New face at the tailboard. Climb up, the dust is worse down there.
You caught me twice. That's rarer than it sounds.
Everything you see has to weigh less by noon. That's my whole problem.
An hour left. I'd sooner sell it cheap than haul it back over the pass.
Light coin is fine by me. Name a number and we'll see what it does.
So. What can I sell you before I'm gone?
PEDDLER.Archetype.Caravan.Lines.tales.0: It's a long road and I've walked most of it.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Caravan.Lines.tales.1: The wind carried a few words my way at the last crossing, and I think you might like to hear 'em.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Caravan.Lines.tales.2: But I don't linger, so don't go looking for me twice in the same place.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Caravan.Lines.fares.0: There's board space behind the crates if you don't mind the jolting.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Caravan.Lines.fares.1: I'm going that way regardless. Costs me nothing but the weight.
You caught me once already, and here we both are again.
Same wagon, fresh stock. Take another look.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Caravan.Lines.charm.0: A little charm for the road, then. Nothing fancy, just something to keep the ruts kind to you.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Caravan.Lines.charm.1: There. Soft earth under your boots.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Caravan.Ambient.browse: Trail goods, mostly. Things that earn their weight when you're days from the nearest town.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Caravan.Lines.no-funds: That's over what you're holding today, friend. Trim it and we'll square up.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Caravan.Lines.gone.0: The pitch is bare. Flattened grass, a cold fire ring, rope ends in the mud.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Caravan.Lines.gone.1: He said he'd be gone by noon. He meant it.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Caravan.Lines.gone.2: The ruts point east and they're still sharp at the edges.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Caravan.Lines.farewell: Thanks for helping keep the wheels turning.
No coin passed, and that's fine. Stop by just to chat next time our paths cross.
Fair winds and clear skies. I'll be down the road by dawn.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Caravan.Choices.greet-: Have you room for a passenger?
Sell me a bit of luck for the road
Didn't I catch you here before?
PEDDLER.Archetype.Caravan.Choices.fw-end: Be gone by morning, then. Take care.
PEDDLER.Archetype.GeneralStore.Name: The Odd Shelf
PEDDLER.Archetype.GeneralStore.Lines.cou: Rope's left. Nails at the back.
Ask if you can't find it.
PEDDLER.Archetype.GeneralStore.Ambient.s: If it works I stock it. Tags are the price.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Tavern.Name: The Adventurers Alcove
Well hello, love! Come in, come in, mind the wet floor by the hearth!
New face, eh? Sit yourself down, I'll pour you something warm.
There you are, {{actor.name}}. Took your time, duck.
You've drunk enough under my roof to count as furniture, you have.
Late one, is it. Fire's banked but there's warmth in it yet.
Now. Drink, a bed, or the news?
PEDDLER.Archetype.Tavern.Lines.rumours.0: They say the old bridge road's washed out again and the caravans are hiring guards. Easy coin, if you've the stomach for mud.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Tavern.Lines.rumours.1: Whole town's uneasy, duck. Folk swear the manor lights burn all night now, and nobody's seen the steward in a fortnight.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Tavern.Lines.rumours.2: Nobody says it above a whisper anymore. What's coming down from the hills isn't bandits, and the garrison knows it.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Tavern.Lines.rumours.3: Same as always, love. Somebody owes somebody, somebody's sweet on somebody, and the ale's a copper too dear.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Tavern.Lines.room.0: Your coin's no good tonight. You've paid for that room ten times over.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Tavern.Lines.room.1: Second door on the left, love. Fresh straw, and the window latches if you jiggle it.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Tavern.Lines.room.2: Sleep soft. I'll not have anyone up those stairs that shouldn't be.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Tavern.Ambient.browse: Ale, wine, a bite of what's on the fire. Point at what you fancy, duck.
Your purse won't cover that one, love. Pick something kinder.
Use it well, duck. And come back thirsty.
Door's where you left it, love.
Keep your head down out there.
PEDDLER.Archetype.MagicShop.Name: The Secondhand Patron
PEDDLER.Archetype.MagicShop.Lines.greeti: A new face, and how delightful. Browse, browse, the good pieces reward a slow eye.
Ah, {{actor.name}}. Returned to good taste, I see.
Do keep the coppers well away from the sapphires, darling. They sulk.
Now. Whatever your eye lands on, it has excellent judgment. What can I show you?
PEDDLER.Archetype.MagicShop.Choices.case: Take my training in the arcane. I'll take the relic.
PEDDLER.Archetype.MagicShop.Choices.gree: Show me what the glass is hiding.
I have something for you to look at
PEDDLER.Archetype.MagicShop.Ambient.brow: Every piece here is charmed, warded, or worse. Do mind which is which.
PEDDLER.Archetype.MagicShop.Lines.locked: The glass doesn't open for coin, darling. Name what you want, then tell me what you'll stop knowing.
PEDDLER.Archetype.MagicShop.Relic.Name: The Secondhand Patron's Relic
PEDDLER.Archetype.MagicShop.Relic.Descri: Bought from the case with something that used to be knowledge.
PEDDLER.Archetype.MagicShop.Ambient.lock: These would embarrass the shelves, so they live behind glass. Touch the velvet. Leave the glass alone.
PEDDLER.Archetype.MagicShop.Lines.no-fun: Oh, sweet thing. That one is rather beyond us today. Choose again, and choose smaller.
PEDDLER.Archetype.MagicShop.Lines.apprai: You brought me something. How thrilling.
Set it on the velvet and take your hand well away. Let the glass do the talking.
A trifling fee for my eye, of course. Nothing that isn't worth it.
PEDDLER.Archetype.MagicShop.Choices.appr: Go on, then. Have your look.
On second thought, keep your fee.
PEDDLER.Archetype.MagicShop.Lines.apprai: The glass sings for it, and it never flatters. This is genuine, and worth a good deal more than whoever sold it to you let on.
You have an eye. That's what the case opens for, and not for many.
The glass stays quiet, and I won't lie to you to fill the silence. It might be enchanted, it might be a very convincing paperweight.
Bring it back when the moon turns and I'll look again.
PEDDLER.Archetype.MagicShop.Lines.farewe: Wear it in the best of health, darling.
Your taste will catch up to your eye. Give it a decade.
Take all the time you like deciding. I'll be here.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Bookseller.Name: The Tome of Tomes
PEDDLER.Archetype.Bookseller.Lines.greet: Oh. Hello. Some weather we're having, isn't it.
Welcome to the Tome of Tomes. I don't think I've seen you in before, so just shout if a spine catches your eye.
Good to see you again. Back for something in particular, or just after the smell of old paper?
Three commissions in my ledger under your name. I'd say we're past small talk.
No rush on coin. Half my regulars only ever come to read the spines, so you're in good company.
So. What sort of thing are you chasing today? You can just tell me, if it helps.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Bookseller.Choices.gre: Back for the usual, if you have it
Could you copy a book for me?
Not sure what I want, honestly
Let me just tell you what I'm after…
PEDDLER.Archetype.Bookseller.Ambient.boo: Take your time. Everything worth reading is a little out of order on purpose.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Bookseller.Lines.no-fu: Ah. That sits outside today's arithmetic, I'm afraid. Set it down gently and we'll try a humbler shelf.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Bookseller.Lines.commi: Ah, a commission. Now that's my favorite kind of afternoon.
Every page by hand, mind, so it takes what it takes. The price is the hours and the ink.
Leave me the title and come back in a few days. I do good work when nobody rushes me.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Bookseller.Choices.com: I'll leave the title with you.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Bookseller.Lines.colle: It is, yes. Bound it in calf, I hope that suits, the goat stock had a smell to it.
Take it away before I start reading it again and decide to keep it.
Not yet, I'm afraid. Ink needs time to dry and I need time to work. Come back later.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Bookseller.Lines.lore-: Histories, good choice. People call them dry, but a decent chronicle is just gossip that outlived everyone in it.
I keep the town annals in the back, sorted by which magistrate was lying that decade.
Two of them the council would rather I had burned. I did not burn them.
Keep your voice exactly where it is.
One is a tithe ledger from the bad winter. It lists what the manor took and, further down, who starved.
The other is a marriage record that makes entirely the wrong man an heir.
I won't sell you either one. But you know they exist now, and that cost you nothing.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Bookseller.Choices.ban: Show me what you will sell.
I didn't hear any of that.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Bookseller.Lines.lore-: Arcana. Careful with that shelf, some of these I keep behind glass for a reason.
I can't cast a lick myself, but I can tell you which of them won't singe your eyebrows off. That counts as a service.
Hm. Not sure I've got exactly that. But I've got a lot, and I'm terrible at throwing things out, so we might have something close.
Give me the subject and a minute, and I'll go rummaging.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Bookseller.Lines.farew: Thank you, truly. I hope it treats you well.
Keep me in mind if you're ever after a good read. Or a bad one, I have those too.
The door sticks. Put a shoulder in it.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Stable.Name: The Muddy Hoof
Ain't seen your face round here before. Watch your boots, the yard's a mite muddy.
Well hey there, {{actor.name}}! Back for another look?
Third horse off this yard for you now. Folks'll start thinking I'm your uncle.
Come on in and take a wander. Every one of 'em's sound in wind and limb, I'll swear to it.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Stable.Ambient.mounts: Take your time picking. You'll be spending a lot of miles with whichever one you take.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Stable.Lines.short.0: Whoa now. That's more horse than you're holding.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Stable.Lines.short.1: Happens to everyone. The plainer stock carries you the same distance.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Stable.Lines.tack-intr: Now, a bare back'll do you no favors past the first mile.
You bought the horse off me, so the leather goes to you at cost. That's how I do it.
While you're here, cast an eye over the tack. Good leather saves you a sore seat.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Stable.Ambient.tack: Oiled and mended, every strap of it. I don't hang anything here I wouldn't ride out on myself.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Stable.Lines.tack-shor: That's dearer than you want. Take the plain set and ride happy.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Stable.Lines.board.0: Now she's yours, where's she laying her head tonight?
PEDDLER.Archetype.Stable.Lines.board.1: I've got a warm stall going spare. {fee} a night, hay and a rubdown thrown in.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Stable.Lines.board.2: Beats leaving her tied to a post in the cold, don't it?
PEDDLER.Archetype.Stable.Lines.confirm.0: She'll be waiting in the stall come morning, fed and brushed. You've my word.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Stable.Lines.confirm.1: That's you all squared away, then.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Stable.Lines.confirm.2: No harm done, come see me when you're in the market for a good horse.
Suit yourself. The gate's always open.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Stable.Lines.fares.0: Not looking to own one, just to get somewhere? I run horses out to a few places.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Stable.Lines.fares.1: Say the word and one of my lads takes the reins. You just hold on.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Fence.Name: The Cloak and Barter
PEDDLER.Archetype.Fence.Lines.greeting.1: New face. Faces are a risk in here.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Fence.Lines.prove.0: You want in deeper. Everyone does.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Fence.Lines.prove.1: Coin first. Then I show you the good shelf.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Fence.Lines.trust-up.1: Don't make me regret the ink.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Fence.Ambient.browse: Front-of-stall stock, nothing that'll get either of us hanged. Look, don't finger it.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Fence.Ambient.browse-f: The quiet stock. Every piece has a story and a price. You never saw where it came from.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Fence.Ambient.unload: Lay it on the cloth. I don't ask, you don't tell.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Fence.Lines.took-it.0: Gone by morning. The story with it.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Fence.Lines.took-it.1: You've a better name in here now.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Fence.Lines.no-funds.0: Wrong price bracket. Set it down.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Fence.Lines.farewell.1: Lane's that way. Walk it separate.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Fence.Choices.greet-pr: How do I earn a real look?
PEDDLER.Archetype.Blacksmith.Ambient.sha: Right, which one am I honing? Set it on the block.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Blacksmith.Blurb: A blunt, proud smith. Haggle her sharpening fee in dialogue, then pick the blade she puts an edge on.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Apothecary.Blurb: An anxious apprentice who never stops talking. Answer what ails you, then hand her a flask to fortify.
PEDDLER.Archetype.GeneralStore.Blurb: A shopkeeper of few words. The smallest tree, with a counter and shelves.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Tavern.Blurb: A warm innkeeper. Rumours track your campaign's act, and a long tab earns a free bed.
PEDDLER.Archetype.MagicShop.Blurb: A theatrical dealer. Roll a table to appraise what you brought, and the locked case opens if it is genuine.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Bookseller.Blurb: A scribe who rambles. Type what you are after, and he keeps a ledger of your commissions.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Stable.Blurb: A folksy horse-trader. Buy a mount first, then tack at cost, then board.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Fence.Blurb: A wary receiver. Climb three rungs of trust, then sell him what you would rather not explain.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Festival.Blurb: A crier who barks the same pitch every time. Open only on market days.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Caravan.Blurb: A trader gone by noon. He counters your offer if you haggle, and the pitch is empty after.
PEDDLER.GM.BlankShopBlurb: An empty shop with a starter tree, opened straight into the editor.

PEDDLER.Stock.DefaultStockHint: Infinite makes every item in this shop unlimited by default. A restock row's own Infinite checkbox still applies either way.

PEDDLER.Identity.GeneralStore.Refuse: That's more than you've got, friend.
PEDDLER.Identity.GeneralStore.Revisit: Anything else I can get you?

PEDDLER.Identity.Blacksmith.EmptyShelf: The rack's empty. Come back when the fire's up.

PEDDLER.Identity.Fence.CurtainLocked: Behind the curtain? Not for a face I don't know.

PEDDLER.Identity.Fence.HaggleLost: Try that again and the door's shut for good.
PEDDLER.Identity.Festival.EmptyShelf: Sold out! Come back next year.
PEDDLER.Identity.Festival.Refuse: Ah, short a few. Next year, maybe!
PEDDLER.Identity.Festival.ClosedLine: Come back when the lanterns are lit.
PEDDLER.Identity.Festival.Cry: Step right up, step right up!
PEDDLER.Identity.Festival.Revisit: Back for more? What else, what else!
PEDDLER.Identity.Festival.HaggleWon: Ha, deal! Step right up next time too!
PEDDLER.Identity.Festival.HaggleLost: Ah, short a few. Come back richer!
PEDDLER.Identity.Festival.Colophon: Gone by sundown, back next year
PEDDLER.Identity.Apothecary.Refuse: That won't stretch to a tonic.
PEDDLER.Identity.Apothecary.HaggleWon: Fine. Take it, and rest easy.
PEDDLER.Identity.Apothecary.HaggleLost: That won't stretch to a tonic. Not today.
PEDDLER.Identity.Bookseller.Refuse: That's a scholar's price, I'm afraid.
PEDDLER.Identity.Bookseller.HaggleWon: Very well. Have it inscribed at your price.
PEDDLER.Identity.Bookseller.HaggleLost: The price is bound as tightly as the book.
PEDDLER.Identity.Caravan.EmptyShelf: That's the lot. The rest went at the last stop.
PEDDLER.Identity.Caravan.Cry: Wares while they last — I'm not stopping long.
PEDDLER.Identity.Caravan.Revisit: Still here? So am I, for now.
PEDDLER.Identity.Caravan.HaggleWon: Fine, fine — wheels don't wait anyway.
PEDDLER.Identity.Caravan.HaggleLost: Then it goes with me. Wheels don't wait.
PEDDLER.Identity.Caravan.Colophon: Here till noon, then already gone
PEDDLER.Identity.MagicShop.HeadSell: Let me see what you have
PEDDLER.Identity.MagicShop.Refuse: I'd want coin up front for that.
PEDDLER.Identity.MagicShop.Revisit: Something else you'd like looked at?
PEDDLER.Identity.MagicShop.HaggleLost: I'd want coin up front for that. Full coin.
PEDDLER.Identity.Stable.Refuse: Not on what's in your purse.
PEDDLER.Identity.Stable.HaggleLost: Not on what's in your purse, I'm afraid.
PEDDLER.Identity.Stable.Colophon: Sound to the gate, no further
PEDDLER.Identity.Tavern.Refuse: That's more than your purse has in it, love.
PEDDLER.Identity.Tavern.Revisit: Another round, or was that it?
PEDDLER.Identity.Tavern.HaggleWon: Ha! Fine — put it on the slate.
PEDDLER.Identity.Tavern.HaggleLost: Your purse is lighter than your thirst, love.
PEDDLER.Sheet.FlavorHint: Short remarks the shopkeeper makes at random while the player fills the counter.
PEDDLER.Sheet.FlavorChanceHint: The odds of a remark on any one pick, from 0 to 1. The totals below speak regardless of this chance.
PEDDLER.Sheet.FlavorThresholdHint: Each total speaks once a visit, when the counter first passes it. Figures are in the primary currency.
PEDDLER.Sheet.FlavorLinePlaceholder: Good pick. That one moves fast.
That's a company's worth of edge.
Either you're arming a war band or you're frightened. Neither's my business.
Mind the stopper on that one, it's a bad seal.
Two drops. Two. Not a mouthful.
Keep it out of the sun or it turns cloudy and useless.
Oh, good, that one actually works, I've seen it work.
Shake it first. Sorry. Shake it first, I always forget to say.
That's the last of that batch, so, um, no pressure.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Apothecary.Flavor.remo: Wise, honestly, it doesn't keep past the month.
Back in the rack, no bother.
Was it the smell? It's usually the smell.
Okay. Okay. We'll find something better.
That's a lot of bandaging for one person.
You're stocking for something bad, aren't you. You don't have to tell me.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Tavern.Flavor.add.3: On the fire since noon, that has.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Tavern.Flavor.big.0: You're settling in for the night, I see.
PEDDLER.Archetype.MagicShop.Flavor.add.0: Oh, that one's been watching you back.
PEDDLER.Archetype.MagicShop.Flavor.remov: It'll keep, darling. Nothing here is in a hurry.
PEDDLER.Archetype.MagicShop.Flavor.big.1: You're going to need a bigger bag, darling, and possibly a lawyer.
PEDDLER.Archetype.MagicShop.Flavor.big.2: At this point I should ask what you intend. I shan't, but I should.
A fine edition. Handle it by the boards, not the spine.
That one has been sat there waiting for somebody for eleven years.
Careful, the ink on that plate never fully took.
Oh, the marginalia in that one is better than the text.
Its previous owner disagreed with the author. Loudly. In pencil.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Bookseller.Flavor.remo: It wasn't for you. No shame in that.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Stable.Flavor.add.2: Check the girth before you ride out.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Stable.Flavor.remove.1: Nothing wrong with second thoughts round a horse.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Stable.Flavor.remove.2: She'd not have liked you anyway.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Stable.Flavor.big.0: That's half my yard walking out the gate.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Stable.Tack.Flavor.add: Good leather. Your backside will thank me.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Fence.Flavor.big.0: That's a lot of trouble in one bundle.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Festival.Flavor.add.1: Oh, that one's lucky, that is.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Festival.Flavor.add.2: Off the wagon this morning, still warm!
PEDDLER.Archetype.Festival.Flavor.add.3: Good eye on you, love, good eye!
PEDDLER.Archetype.Festival.Flavor.big.0: Look at the arms on you, carrying all that!
PEDDLER.Archetype.Festival.Flavor.big.1: You'll not get that lot home without eating half!
PEDDLER.Archetype.Caravan.Flavor.add.0: Carried that over two passes. It can carry itself now.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Caravan.Flavor.add.1: You'll want that before the border.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Caravan.Flavor.add.2: Good weight off the axle, that.
Back in the crate it goes, then.
That's more for me to haul.
You're breaking my heart and my axle.
Suit yourself. It goes over the pass with me.
I'd have gone lower on that, you know.
PEDDLER.Archetype.Caravan.Flavor.big.0: Now that's a wagon getting lighter. Keep going.

PEDDLER.Library.Line.2: Door's open. You came in. So.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.3: Oh, it's you again, love! Good, good!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.4: Look who it is! Come for more, have you?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.5: Get IN here and give us a hug, you!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.6: Oh thank the heavens, a real friend, sit, the kettle's on!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.7: What'll it be, love? Everything's fresh, I don't do stale.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.8: Hungry, are you? Course you are, look at the spread!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.9: Your usual, duck? Already wrapping it!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.10: Knew you'd be in! Saved you the good corner loaf!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.11: First time, love? Oh you're in for it, sit down, taste this.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.12: Never been in? Where've you BEEN, come, try the honey buns.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.13: ...Didn't expect your sort down this lane.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.14: An honor. I think. State what you came for.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.15: Fellow tradesfolk, eh? Then you know good work when you taste it!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.16: Ah, one of us! Come round the back, the real stock's there.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.17: ...You I know. Keep your hands where the light is.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.18: We're the same animal, you and me. So no games.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.19: Up with me, are you, love! Bread's not even cooled!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.20: Morning, duck! First batch is yours, still warm, go on!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.21: Afternoon, love! Caught the lunch lot, did you!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.22: Middle of the day and half sold out, lucky you came!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.23: Oh love, it's late, but for you there's still a heel of bread!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.24: Past closing, duck, but I never turn away a hungry face, come in.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.25: THERE you are! Oh, my day's made, it is!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.26: Oh love, come here, I've missed your face something rotten!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.28: I'll deal with you. Doesn't mean I like it.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.29: Enjoy it warm, love, that's how it's meant!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.30: Off you pop! And no sharing, you earned that loaf!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.31: No bother, love, come back when your belly grumbles!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.32: Off you go then! The smell alone'll bring you back, mark me.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.33: Don't you dare be a stranger, you hear!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.34: Go on, love, and come round Sunday, I'll bake your favorite!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.37: Right, love, the oven's calling, but lovely seeing you!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.38: I'd better get back before it burns, off you go, duck!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.39: That's me done, love. Out you get.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.40: Right, enough chat, I've bread to mind. Bye now.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.41: Take a loaf for the road, love, you'll thank me!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.42: Safe home, duck, and eat something proper out there!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.43: You come back to me in one piece, you hear, I'll have cake!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.44: Go get 'em, love! And mind yourself, I mean it!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.45: Can't decide, love? Tell me you're hungry and I'll do the rest!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.46: Anything you fancy, just point, I'll have it bagged before you blink!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.47: Just looking, love? Look away, the smell's free!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.48: No coin today? No bother, come back when there is.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.51: Up before the birds I was, for that crust, you won't taste better!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.52: Real butter in that, love, none of your cheap fat, you can tell!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.53: Ooh, that's the wedding cake, love, bit dear, but this bun's just as lovely!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.54: Save your coppers, duck, the day-old's half price and just as sweet.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.56: ...You can't afford the dust on that. Move along.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.57: Price stands. I don't barter twice.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.59: ...Oh, go on then, but you'll not tell a soul!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.60: Fine, fine, a copper off, you cheeky thing, take it!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.61: Tell you what, love, buy two and I'll round it down!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.62: I'll not budge on the loaf, but I'll toss in a roll, how's that!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.63: All gone, love! Sold out by noon, that's how good it is!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.64: Oh, you're too late, duck, the last went an hour past, come early next!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.65: Bless you, love, I bake bread, not whatever that is!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.66: That's not a bakery thing, duck, try the grocer two doors down!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.67: ...Love, that grain's gone off, I'll not take it.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.68: Oh no, duck, that's past saving, even my pigs would turn their noses.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.69: ...Where'd you get a sack like that, love? No. I don't want it.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.70: That's someone's mark on the sack, duck. Take it back where it came from.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.71: Ooh, careful, love, leave that be, eh?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.72: Hands off the display, duck, there's a love.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.74: No, love. I said no. Put it down.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.75: Stop. You're making noise. I hate noise.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.76: ...Put it down before this gets loud.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.77: ...Please, love, don't, there's no need for this.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.78: Easy now, easy, you don't want to do this, please.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.79: You'll stop right there, my lad, or I'll stop you!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.80: That's quite enough! Stand still, the lot of you!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.81: Oh, I can't do that one, love, sorry as I am.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.82: Wish I could help, duck, but that's beyond me.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.84: Not happening, duck. Don't ask twice.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.85: ...You came to my shop to ask THAT.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.86: Get out. That question alone could get you killed.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.87: Right, love, I think you've had your fill, off you pop!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.88: Time to be going, duck, the door's right there!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.89: Out, love. Now. Before I come round this counter!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.90: You'll leave on your feet or I'll see you leave another way, last chance!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.91: ...Nothing's that cheap and honest, love, what's the catch!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.92: Ho, if it's that good a deal, duck, someone's getting cheated, and it's not me!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.95: ...You did me a real turn. I don't forget those. Ever.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.96: I owe you. In my world that means something. It means everything.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.97: ...Fine. Thank you. Don't get used to hearing it.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.98: I owe you. Hate that. But I owe you.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.99: Ooh, my mistake, love, here, let me sort it!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.100: Sorry, duck, butterfingers, one moment, I'll fix it!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.101: ...I wronged you. In my line, that's rare to admit. I'm saying it.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.102: That was on me. Tell me the price of fixing it.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.103: Oh hush, love, it's forgotten, come have a slice!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.104: Don't you fret, duck, all's mended, sit down!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.106: Fine, love. But I've a long memory, mind.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.107: ...Sorry's just a word, love, and it's not enough.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.108: No. Some things a sorry won't bake out, duck.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.109: Which way's the mill, love? I've gone and turned about!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.110: Point me to the square, duck, I'm all flour-headed today!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.111: Eh? Say that again, love, the oven's loud!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.112: Once more, duck, I didn't catch it over the kneading!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.113: Do us a favor, love, would you?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.114: I need a hand, duck, and you're the one I'd trust with it.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.115: Sorry to trouble you, love, could you lend a hand?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.116: You look strong, duck, fancy helping an old baker a moment?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.117: Soft now, love, the little ones are napping in the back.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.118: Ooh, gentle voices, duck, there's a love.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.119: Keep it down, love, I can hear you from the ovens!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.120: Lower your voice, duck, you'll curdle the milk!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.121: MIND YOURSELVES, hot bread coming through!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.122: Make way, loves, make way, mind the trays!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.123: Pst, love, over here, quick word.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.124: Here, duck, come close, don't make a fuss.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.125: Oh love, that's WONDERFUL, I could dance!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.126: Get away! That's grand news, duck, this calls for cake!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.128: ...Right. Then we move before it gets worse.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.129: Ha! Heard worse from my own bread when it won't rise, love!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.130: Oh, is that meant to sting, duck? Bless your little heart.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.131: ...That weren't kind, love. That weren't kind at all.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.132: ...Oh. Right. Well. That one got me, duck, it did.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.133: ...You'll die owing money to people meaner than me.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.134: At least my reputation's worth something. Yours is just warnings.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.135: Threaten ME, in MY bakery? Ho, you've picked the wrong old woman, love!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.136: I've chased off worse than you with a wooden spoon, duck, try me!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.137: ...Alright, alright, love, no need, here, take the till, just go.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.138: Easy now, easy, I'll not fight you, please, love.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.139: ...Something's coming. I can smell the watch on the wind.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.140: ...My doors stay locked tonight. Something's wrong.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.141: Ugh, get that OUT, love, it'll turn the milk!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.142: Faugh! What is that, duck, take it away before I'm sick!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.143: ...You're being awful sweet, love. Sweeter than my buns. Why's that.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.144: Hmph. I know a butter-up when I hear one, duck. What're you after.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.145: Walk away now, love, and we'll both forget it.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.146: I'm asking you the once, duck, kindly, leave.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.147: ...I know which window is yours. Sleep on that.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.148: Cross me and you'll vanish so quiet the birds won't notice.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.149: Get OUT before I take the rolling pin to your THICK skull!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.150: I'll bake YOU into a pie, you wretch, OUT!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.151: Bless you, love, you tried, didn't you.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.152: Face like a dropped scone, you've got, duck.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.153: ...No wonder your own kin don't come round, love.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.154: You've curdled every good thing you've ever touched, duck, and you know it.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.155: ...Pah, you're not worth the flour to throw at you, love.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.156: I've bread rising, I've no time for the likes of you, duck.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.157: ...You win, love, you win, I'm sorry, please.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.158: ...Alright, I'm done, I'm done, just leave it be, duck.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.159: ...Watch. Quietly. Trouble at the curio shop.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.160: Guards. There. And tell them nothing about me.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.161: Rain's coming, love, my bad knee never lies about that.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.162: Grey old sky, duck, good day for staying in with warm bread, eh!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.163: Quiet morning, love, just me and the dough for company.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.164: Slow day, duck, gives me time to natter, lucky you!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.165: You've a good heart, love, anyone can see it plain.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.166: You did that proper, duck, I'm proud of you, I am.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.167: Strong arms on you, love! Here, fancy carrying these trays for a free bun?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.168: Oh you're a clever one, duck, just the sort I need for a little errand.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.169: ...Don't say I said, love, but the butcher's behind on his rent.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.170: Word round the square, duck, is the magistrate's looking for a new clerk, and why.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.171: So go on, love, what's the talk round the well this morning?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.172: Anything juicy, duck? You always hear it before I do!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.173: ...That's not for spreading, love, mouths shut in my shop.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.174: I'll not have that talk by my ovens, duck. Enough.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.175: Anyway, love, you came for bread, not chatter, what'll it be!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.176: Ooh, that reminds me, duck, have you tried the new seed loaf!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.177: ...We'll not speak of that, love. What did you want.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.179: ...Loss is loss. Sit. No one's watching here.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.180: ...Nothing to say. So I'll just keep the door for you a while.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.181: ...You've weathered storms before, love, and here you stand.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.182: One thing at a time, duck, I'll help you carry it, I will.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.183: ...Tell old Bru what's wrong, love, and we'll sort it together.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.184: You'll not face this alone, duck, not while I've an oven and a door.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.185: ...I'll help. And one day I'll knock, and you'll answer. Deal?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.186: ...Done. But you're in my book now. I always collect.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.187: ...I don't sell things. I sell silence. The things are free.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.188: ...Everyone's got a door they don't want opened. I keep keys.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.190: State your business or move along.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.192: Thought I might see you again. People do.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.193: ...You can talk in here. It's safe. Mostly.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.194: Sit where I can see the lane. Then we talk.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.195: Take your time. Touch nothing without asking.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.196: Whatever you need, maybe I have it. Maybe.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.197: Back again. Knew you would be.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.199: Don't know your face. That's not nothing, here.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.200: First time. Then you don't know the rules yet. Watch.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.202: An honor. What do you require.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.203: You know how this works. So we skip the dance.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.204: One professional to another. Quick and quiet.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.206: Look all you like. Pocket nothing.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.207: Early. Honest folk aren't up yet.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.208: This hour, only two kinds out. Which are you.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.209: Lot of eyes about at this hour. Be brief.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.212: Late callers want the quiet stock. Come in.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.214: Was hoping for your knock and no one else's.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.218: Walk a separate way from the door. Habit.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.221: Watch the lane on your way.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.225: Anyway, um, I should probably, the shelves won't restock themselves.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.226: Sorry, I, I've got to get back to it, but this was nice!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.227: Okay, I really, I have to go, sorry, bye.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.228: I, I can't keep talking, I'm sorry, I just can't right now.

PEDDLER.Library.Line.987: Ye've got me beat! I yield, let me sit a spell and we'll talk.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.988: Oi'! Where's the militia, some skull's need knockin' over here!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.989: Pleasant rain! Always gives me a better yield.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.990: Calm sun and a cool breeze, nothin' quite like it.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.991: Bit too chilly - not near as much to do once the frost hits.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.992: What a storm! We've weathered worse and it's good to clear out the old growth!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.993: Hm. I don't get out much, got any other rumour to share?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.994: Honest and true, the list of people I like more than plants is short. It honours me t' ad ye to it.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.995: Y' got a sharp eye! Take a look o'er here, I got somethin' that might suit ye.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.996: The wind carried a few words my way; I think ye might like to hear em.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.997: What's all that hubbub goin' round town?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.998: No, I think ye must've misheard. Only fools fall prey to that kind o' jabber.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.999: Maybe, but - oh! Darn it!! Skewered me thumb again. Can you pass me that cloth o'er there? These damn shears. Next time yer by the smith, can you ask him if he'll sharpen 'em for free? His work dulls so fast...
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1000: Ah, pick somethin' else t' talk about. I ain't here for that chatter.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1001: Oh, dear. Ill fate befalls us all, but I'm sorry t' hear. I have some tinctures that could numb that wound for ye.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1002: Trust your feet to carry ye to good fate, dear.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1003: Slow down dear! I'm happy to help, just give me a breath and I'll lend a hand.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1004: I'd love to help, but I've a lot on my mind... Perhaps we could trade favours?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1008: {Randomly compliment something about the character speaking to them}
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1012: Now just what are you up to, {CHARACTER}?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1013: Oh, {CHARACTER}! Good timing, I was just thinking about you.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1014: (in a silly accent) Got some good things on sale, stranger... (giggle) Sorry, I couldn't help it! I've been reading a very fun book, you see...
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1017: Look what the cat dragged in!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1019: Well well well, look who's here.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1022: Please browse the stocks however you like.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1026: Hi, {CHARACTER} - looking for {item they purchase regularly/accessory related to previous purchase}? We moved the shop around, it'll be {new location in area}.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1027: If it isn't my favorite {CHARACTER}! Hey, we just got in {item related to their class}. Might be helpful?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1028: Oh, {CHARACTER}! Want some of my candy? I think I bought too much.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1029: Hey, newcomer! Welcome to {SHOP NAME}. What's on the list today?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1030: How can I help you? Anything special on the mind?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1031: Well, I haven't seen you here before! Welcome to {SHOP NAME} - how can I help you?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1033: Welcome to {SHOP NAME}, milord/milady/{NOBLE TITLE + CHARACTER NAME}.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1034: Please let me know if you need anything, I'll have it fetched.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1035: {Does not greet. Stares in mild panic/disdain, dealer's choice on which.}
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1036: G'day! Got some interesting stock in today. Care to look?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1037: Thanks for waiting - bit busy today, never a dull moment here. What do you need?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1038: How're you feeling? Have you eaten yet today?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1039: You look exhausted. When was the last time you slept?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1040: I'm glad to see you again. Oh, I just finished making lunch, would you like to share it with me?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1041: It looks like it might get cold tonight. Do you have a place to stay?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1042: Your clothes look a little worn... let me see if I have my sewing kit, I'll mend them.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1043: Good morning! Come on in. I've just put tea on, want a cup?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1044: Ah, that crisp morning air... oops! Sorry, I didn't see you there. Welcome!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1045: -hums a bit of a song- Ah! When did you...? I'm still waking up, sorry. What would you like?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1046: Afternoon! My, time does fly doesn't it? Feels like the day's already over...
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1047: Good afternoon! Sheesh, can today move any slower?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1048: Good day - have you eaten lunch yet? I just finished mine, but I can always make more.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1049: -yawn- Good evening... where did the day go?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1050: Good evening - you're still working this late? Working hard is all well and good, but maybe consider a nap.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1051: T'is the witching hour, I hear. Perhaps you should turn in for the night?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1052: What has you up so late, {CHARACTER}? Promise me you'll get some sleep soon.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1053: {CHARACTER}! Always a pleasure. I've got some of that candy you liked, should you feel peckish.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1054: There's my {CHARACTER}! I was wondering when you'd get in. You've eaten today, haven't you? I'll look the other way if you happen to need a snack.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1055: I was just thinking about you, {CHARACTER}. Let me put some tea on.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1057: How may I help you today?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1058: Take care out there! If you have any problems, let me know!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1059: Be safe on your way to {LOCATION}!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1062: Be safe on your way home, all right?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1063: Feel free to stop in just to chat any time.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1065: Now, don't you get hurt out there! I'll come after Hades himself with my rolling pin if he puts a hand on you.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1066: Oh, be sure to come back before you leave! I'll want to say goodbye.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1070: Apologies, but I need to get back to work - why don't you swing by later once I'm less busy? I can talk then!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1071: Ah, look at me rambling - I apologize, I should let you get back to brass tacks. Shout if you need me!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1072: All right, that's enough. Conversation's over.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1073: I need to get back to work. If you don't need anything else...
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1074: I'm sorry, but I'm burning daylight and need to focus on work now.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1075: Be safe out there! When you come back, I'll make something delicious for you.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1076: Come back in one piece or I'll bring whatever hurt you back in pieces!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1077: Fair winds and clear skies, dearie.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1079: I know you'll do fine, but I'm crossing my fingers for you anyway.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1080: Bravado and bolster, stormwind at your back - you'll be okay. I know you will.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1081: Got something in particular you're looking for?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1082: What're you doing today? I might have something to help.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1083: Just window shoppin' or need a bit of help?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1084: Take your time. I'm glad for the company, really.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1085: Hm, stock's a bit low today. Maybe try back later in the week after I get a shipment in?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1086: Oh! {OTHER SHOP NAME} down the road might have something more helpful. Tell the owner I say hello, won't you?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1088: This is really annoying to get, if I'm being honest - if you'd like to get it yourself, I can tell you who my supplier is or where to find it in the wild, but if you need it /now/ this'll be the cheapest way.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1089: I suppose the cost is a bit high, but if I don't set it that way I can't keep them on the shelf long enough for everyone who needs one to get one! I'm sure there's cheaper ones, but they'll break much faster at that price point.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1090: No, I agree it's quite high - but I can't get ahold of it for any cheaper and we can't produce them in house, and everyone seems to want them. I'm sorry. Maybe come back a bit later when supply's better?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1091: I don't think you need something like this right now - maybe in the future, though!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1092: The only people who buy this are ones with more money than sense and I think you might be smarter than your purse suggests. Let me find you something that'll be more cost effective.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1093: This is too expensive for most of my clients to afford, I really only keep it as a show piece at this point. Let me show you something a little sturdier.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1094: This isn't going to be worth either of our time, I'm afraid. Let's find you something you'll get more use out of.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1095: I'm sorry, but this is going to be out of your price range. The material cost alone is ridiculous...
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1096: You don't need something like this, promise. Here, let me help you find something more helpful.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1097: That's the price, I won't go lower.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1098: I'm already breaking even at this point, I can't go lower. I'm sorry.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1099: Hm, if this is out of your range, maybe I can ask one of my friends a town over to keep an eye out for you.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1100: Absolutely not, I'm sorry, this took too much work to make/get. I won't go lower.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1101: It seems you need this much more than I do. I'll accept that price.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1102: Hmm... you know, I think I could stand to part with this anyway.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1103: I think I can afford to swallow my pride on this one. Deal.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1104: I really need to re-evaluate this price if it's that bad. I'll take it.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1106: I don't think I can quite go THAT low! But {PRICE} I can manage. How's that?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1107: This is going to be quite the pain to resupply - can you do {PRICE}?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1108: Normally I would say no, but you're not far off the lowest I go. Does {PRICE} work for you?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1109: Sorry, {CHARACTER}. I ran out a bit ago...
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1110: Apologies, but we had a bit of a rush. I'm fresh out.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1111: Check back in a week or so, I fear I've run dry on that.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1112: Hm, that's an interesting request! Sadly it's not something I carry.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1113: I may not have it, but I know {OTHER SHOP} might. Try them?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1114: Maybe you'll be better served looking elsewhere, I fear that's beyond my ken!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1115: I fear this won't be something I can carry, but I imagine {OTHER SHOP} may like it.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1116: Now, I'm familiar with the Guild - I've a cousin or two in the second oldest profession, you see - but I can't fence this for you. I've had rather enough trouble with the law.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1117: I'm sorry, this looks a tad too familiar for me. Have you spoken with {THIEF NPC}?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1118: Maybe you should find a more discreet merchant for this, honey.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1119: All right, that's enough fun for one day!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1123: You stop that or I will fetch my rolling pin and -make- it stop.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1124: Keep that up and I fear you'll rather dislike the result.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1125: Th' next devil t' try my patience is goin' to the kraken, express mail!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1126: Did ye use yer ears fer a flax-field? CUT IT OUT!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1128: I can't talk about that right now, I'm sorry.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1129: Please don't make me escalate this. I don't want to.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1130: Don't you think that's too personal a question?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1131: You -do not- want to see what happens if you keep doin' that, lad/lassie/friend.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1132: This stops now or I make it stop permanently.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1133: Don't make me get my rolling pin!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1134: I've too much to do today, I can't. But thank you for thinking of me.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1136: I won't be able to manage that. I'm sorry.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1137: I can't really do that right now.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1138: I have no desire to assist with that.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1140: What do you take me for?!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1141: Ask me that again and you'll end up at the bottom of my well.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1142: I think it's best you head out.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1143: I'm sure you have much to get done. Shall I walk you out?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1144: I wish I could keep chatting, but I'll need to get back to work now. I'll see you some other time!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1145: Get out or they'll drag your corpse out by the short-hairs.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1146: Do -not- push me further or I'll get the rolling pin.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1148: I'm sure this could be all you promise and more... but I think someone else might deserve that even more.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1149: I can't accept this, I'm sorry. I just can't see that being possible without some kind of catch.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1151: That was very kind of you, thank you. Would you like some tea?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1152: I cannot thank you enough. Next time my old friends are in town, come by, we'll treat you.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1153: You've been as kind to me as my own crew was. You're welcome here any time.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1154: I won't deny I owe you for this. Please come by again when you can so we can discuss the terms of me repaying you.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1155: I'm thankful for the assistance. How can I pay you back?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1156: Oops! Seems I might have dipped a bit too much into the stock last night. I'll fix that right up.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1157: Now just how did I pull that off?! Terribly sorry, one moment and I'll fix this up.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1159: What brings you to this part of town?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1161: What trouble did you get into this time?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1162: Welcome in, take a look around. Let me know if you need help with anything or have any questions.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1163: What are you in for this time?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1164: A familiar face on a familiar day, back for your usual?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1165: Welcome to the forge! No I wont try to replicate someone elses work but I am happy to make you something new.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1166: Mind your hands, the swords are sharp.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1168: Pardon my yawn, you're up earlier than the coals are.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1169: You made it before the coals went dark. How can I assist your late night journey?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1170: Been a long time! I was starting to get worried the mountain goats got you.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1171: I was just talking about you, glad to see you could make it!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1172: Thanks for stopping by, may my wares treat you well.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1173: Thanks for stopping by, keep me in mind if you need something made.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1176: Let the ancients light your path.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1177: Don't let the coals burn your feet.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1178: I've gotta get going, but it was nice to chat with you.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1179: I've gotta go, the forge needs some tending.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1180: May the forge bless your travels.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1181: Tend your coals carefully, they will lead your path.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1182: Decisions are hard when there are so many options, any way I can help narrow your search?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1183: Is there something specific you were looking for? Anything I can help with before getting back to my work?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1184: Everything here is handcrafted by me with care. The price reflects the time, skills, and materials put into every artifact.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1185: I work hard for my craft, you can't ask me to devalue my work.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1186: Thats as low as the value can go.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1187: Tell you what, you got a bit of spark. I'll do it for you just this once.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1188: Don't think I can go that low, lets meet somewhere closer to the middle.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1189: That item has been flying off the shelves lately. Sorry to say I haven't had the spare time to make more.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1190: An item like that is a bit out of my skill set. I'm sure someone else in the market might have what you are looking for though.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1191: Theres more value in my scrap bucket than in this, its not worth the time it would take for me to make it usable.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1192: I don't think I can turn over an item such as this, its a bit out of my market.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1193: Stop that, please. I don't want to have to ask again.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1194: If you dont behave yourself I will ask you to leave.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1195: I suggest you stop right now, or I'll have to handle this matter myself (usually while grabbing a hammer or other such tool off a workbench).
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1197: No, absolutely not. Why would you even ask?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1198: Thank you for your time, but we are closing up for a break, so if you would head on out I would appreciate it.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1199: I suggest you get going, before things get any worse.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1200: Only the gods accept that kind of wishful thinking.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1202: (Leaving them a handcrafted gift of something they like)
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1203: Thank you so much, how can I repay you?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1206: I'm so sorry, how can I make it up to you?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1207: Oh its okay, thank you for apologizing.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1208: I'm not ready to forgive you yet, but I appreciate you apologizing for what you did.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1209: No! An apology doesnt just make this better!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1210: Can you tell me how to get there?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1211: Someone up the road told me the old mine was this way, youre saying its not? Well can you prove them wrong and show me the way?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1214: Can you say that one more time, I didnt quite catch it?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1215: Will you do this for me? I'll owe you one.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1216: Would you mind doing X? It'll make things easier for me.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1217: Would you mind your volume please? Youre getting a bit loud right in my ear.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1219: Are you sure you are ready to swing above your weight class? I dont take nicely to being threatened.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1221: Theres plenty of hot coals here if you are looking to take a walk.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1222: Nice weather eh? Shame, its too warm here for my liking.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1223: Bad weather? No it doesnt rain here nearly as much as I wish it did.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1224: Have you heard the fire's whisper?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1225: The flames tell you anything new lately?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1226: We don't go starting wildfires around here.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1227: Whats going on? Who needs their face punched in?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1228: Sure I can give you hand, but my hourly rate isnt cheap.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1229: Hey, some weather we are having, huh?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1230: Good morning/ afternoon/ evening, [Name]. How are you?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1231: What's up [Name]! How have you been?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1232: Welcome to [Place name], how can I help you today.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1233: Welcome to [Place Name], I haven't seen you here before, let me know if there is anything in particular you are looking for.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1236: I don't I just keep an eye on them.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1241: Thank you! I hope you enjoy your [Item name].
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1242: Thank you for stopping by. I hope you come back.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1243: I look forward to seeing you again!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1244: Don't let the door hit you on the way out.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1245: I am sorry to have to do this, but there is something I have to do. Can we pick this up some other time?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1246: Look, I need to go. Have a good day.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1249: Anything I can help you with?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1250: I don't think we have what you are looking for, have you tried looking else where?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1252: This is exactly what you need, and the extra features help justify its quality!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1253: I don't think this is in your budget.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1254: I don't think you can afford this.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1255: I'm sorry, but the price is the price.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1256: Well, when you put it like that...
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1257: I can't do X but I can do Y.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1258: I just sold the last of [Item Name] a little while ago, the restock won't be in till later.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1259: I am afraid we don't carry [Item Name].
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1260: Look, you and I know that this is something I won't buy.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1261: I can't buy that for... ethical reasons...
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1262: Could you please do that somewhere else?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1264: I am about to lose my temper, please stop.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1268: It's getting late, I think you need to get going?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1269: I think you should leave. Now.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1270: I think I'll pass for now.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1272: Thank you. I'll be sure to return the favor someday.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1273: Alright, alright, I'll admit that was helpful.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1275: I apologize, it won't happen again.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1276: It's okay. It wasn't that big of a deal.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1278: I don't forgive you for this.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1279: How do you get to [Place name]?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1280: Hey, could you do [task] for me?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1281: Sorry to bother you, but could you do something for me real quick?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1282: Could you please lower your voice.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1288: Heh, cute, as I was saying...
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1290: Not so funny now is it?
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1291: Are you threatening me? The answer better be no...
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1292: Allright, allright, we are all friends here right? Let's be friends...
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1296: Look, I think you need to go. Now.
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1297: You should consider what I say next very seriously as this is the only time I'll ask...
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1298: Listen here you [Cuss], you better listen or else!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1299: Well, well, well, look who the cat dragged in!
PEDDLER.Library.Line.1300: That is a little too specfic.
PEDDLER.Builder.StockNote: The shelves show whatever {name} carries. Dropping onto {name}'s sheet works too. The Stock tab in Shop Settings sets how often each item comes back.
PEDDLER.Builder.StockDrop: Drop Items or an Item folder here to stock the shop
PEDDLER.Builder.ClearStockConfirm: Remove all {count} items from {name}? This deletes them from the actor.
PEDDLER.Builder.FilterHint: Each row is one filter. Add rows or groups to tighten it, delete rows to loosen it. The small box beside a row's dropdown only searches the list of filters.
PEDDLER.Builder.DraftSaved: Shop draft saved. Open Create Peddler Shop on this actor to pick up where you left off.
PEDDLER.Builder.DraftResumed: Picked up your saved shop draft.
PEDDLER.Builder.StartOverConfirm: Throw away this shop draft and begin again?
PEDDLER.Builder.LibraryMore: {count} more. Narrow the search to see them.

MINSTREL.Settings.SilentMode.Hint: How Minstrel picks between competing combat cues.

MINSTREL.Keybinds.ToggleCombat.Name: Toggle combat music

MINSTREL.Keybinds.ToggleNowPlaying.Hint: Show or hide the now playing bar.
MINSTREL.Keybinds.TransportPrev.Name: Previous track
MINSTREL.Keybinds.TransportPause.Name: Pause or resume
